## Glossary

**check-fix**  
Class: the dagger↔section audit (checkRepo/checkFile) and its repair (fixRepo).

**checkRepo**  
Public: returns CheckViolations for the repo or scoped paths.

**dagger**  
`// gloss` above a declaration, planted by harvest, paired with a section by check.

**escapeHeadings**  
Internal: escapes harvested lines starting with '#' so they cannot fabricate sections.

**findGlossRoot**  
Public: walks up from a directory to the repo root holding gloss.

**fixRepo**  
Public: applies FixActions (renameSection, moveGlossFile, rewriteHeaderPath).

**gloss harvest --staged**  
Pre-commit harvest of staged files; the default write path.

**gloss watch**  
Opt-in save-time harvest, heavily debounced (DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS).

**gloss.exclude**  
package.json path prefixes skipped by harvest, lint, check and fix; segment-boundary match.

**.gloss/**  
The committed mirror tree at the repo root that holds every sidecar.

**.gloss/.events.jsonl**  
Machine-local harvester state; the one gitignored file under .gloss/.

**GlossDoc**  
Parsed sidecar data from parseGlossDoc: source path, preamble, sections.

**glossPathFor**  
Public: maps a repo-relative source path to its sidecar path.

**harvest**  
Class: moving source comments into sidecar sections and planting daggers.

**harvestPaths**  
Public: harvests files on disk under paths and reports counts.

**harvestSource**  
Public: harvests one in-memory source string into a gloss doc.

**headerPathMismatch**  
Check violation: the sidecar's `# <path>` h1 does not match its source path.

**locateGlossFile**  
Public: finds the existing sidecar for a source file.

**markerWithoutSection**  
Check violation: a dagger whose symbol has no section.

**orphanGlossFile**  
Check violation: a sidecar whose source file no longer exists.

**preamble**  
Optional file-level text under the `# <path>` h1; paired with `// gloss:file`.

**section**  
A `## <symbol>` block in a sidecar; the heading is its only binding to code.

**sectionWithoutMarker**  
Check violation: a section whose dagger is gone or whose symbol was renamed.

**sidecar**  
The gloss file for one source file: .gloss/<source path>.md.

**sidecar-format**  
Class: the .gloss/ mirror layout and the markdown format of a gloss file.

**sourcePathFor**  
Public: maps a sidecar path back to its source path; undefined for non-gloss paths.

**upsertSection**  
Public: inserts or replaces one symbol's section in a parsed doc.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The margin file and its lifecycle: the .gloss/ mirror layout and markdown format, the harvester that writes it from source comments, and the bidirectional dagger↔section check and its repair.

## 2. The domain

A sidecar lives at the source path under .gloss/ with .md appended (src/foo.ts → .gloss/src/foo.ts.md) and exists only when the file has something in its margin. It is plain markdown: an `# <source path>` h1, an optional preamble, one `## <symbol>` section per symbol (`Class.method`, `default`). The heading is the entry's only binding; never quote code lines or cite line numbers. For path work use glossPathFor (source → sidecar path), sourcePathFor (back), locateGlossFile (an existing sidecar) and findGlossRoot (the repo root). For content use parseGlossDoc → upsertSection → serializeGlossDoc instead of string-editing markdown.

Harvest is the write path: it sweeps every comment that is not a dagger, directive or why: into its enclosing symbol's section and plants the dagger. From the shell use `gloss harvest` (`--staged` in pre-commit is the calm default) or opt-in `gloss watch` (debounced, never rewrites mid-edit). From code use harvestPaths for files on disk and harvestSource for one in-memory string; watchGloss is internal. gloss.exclude keeps vendored, tracked trees out of every surface. Check/fix keeps the pairing honest: checkRepo (or checkFile for one file) reports markerWithoutSection, sectionWithoutMarker, orphanGlossFile, headerPathMismatch and the rest; fixRepo repairs renames, moved mirrors (via git mv) and header paths. Never delete a section or dagger to green a check.

Not here: what counts as a harvestable comment, the resolver and `gloss lint` (comment-rule-and-source-scanning); rendering a gloss with staleness and its history (read-and-staleness); feeding glosses to agents on Read/Grep and `gloss setup` (agent-integration-setup-and-cli).

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#where-the-gloss-lives -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Where the gloss lives (in "@inixiative/gloss")

#### Where the gloss lives

A mirrored tree at the repo root: every source file's margin is the same path under `.gloss/`, with
`.md` appended.

```
src/lens/applyLens.ts        →  .gloss/src/lens/applyLens.ts.md
src/fieldMap/types.ts        →  .gloss/src/fieldMap/types.ts.md
packages/api/src/hooks.ts    →  .gloss/packages/api/src/hooks.ts.md
```

Enumeration respects `.gitignore`: a gitignored source file (generated SDK clients, build
output) is never linted, harvested, or checked, tracked or not. Outside a git repo the full
tree is walked.

`.gloss/` is committed and reviewed like any docs tree. The one exception is
`.gloss/.events.jsonl` (machine-local harvester state), which setup gitignores. A gloss file exists
only when a source file has something in its margin; comment-free files get no mirror.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#the-sidecar -->
**Source:** `README.md` § The sidecar (in "@inixiative/gloss")

#### The sidecar

Plain markdown, no frontmatter, no schema. An `# <source path>` h1, an optional file preamble, then
one `## <symbol>` section per symbol. Class members key as `Class.method`; `export default` keys as
`default`. Linear and PR references are ordinary markdown links.

An entry that fits on one line is one bullet; anything longer is a paragraph. The `## <symbol>`
heading is the entry's only binding. It is the one link the checker can verify (dagger ↔ section).
A quoted code line or a line number would answer "where does this apply" with a syntactic proxy
that rots silently, so a section names what inside its symbol it means in words, never by line.

```md
# src/resolver.ts

The single marker→symbol resolver. The ESLint rule and the CI check both consume this — two
implementations of "which declaration does this marker belong to" would diverge and produce
lint-passes/CI-fails split-brain.

## resolveMarkerTarget

- a decorator is part of the declaration it decorates

Skips blank lines and other comments between the dagger and the declaration. Rejects
multi-declarator `const a = 1, b = 2` rather than guessing which half was meant. See
[ZLT-1204](https://linear.app/...).

## ParsedSource

`markerLine` is absent for symbols reached without a dagger; the checker uses that to find sections
whose dagger was deleted.
```

<!-- unit doc:.gloss/src/harvest.ts.md#escapeheadings -->
**Source:** `.gloss/src/harvest.ts.md` § escapeHeadings (in "src/harvest.ts")

#### escapeHeadings

a harvested line starting with '#' would parse as gloss structure (h1 path header,
'##' symbol section) and fabricate sections naming no symbol; escape it at column 0.

<!-- unit doc:.gloss/src/harvest.ts.md#entryfor -->
**Source:** `.gloss/src/harvest.ts.md` § entryFor (in "src/harvest.ts")

#### entryFor

the symbol section is gloss's only validated binding — a quoted code line (like a line
number) rots silently and answers "where does this apply" with a syntactic proxy.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#the-harvester -->
**Source:** `README.md` § The harvester (in "@inixiative/gloss")

#### The harvester

The write path is mechanical, not instructional. A comment an agent writes out of habit doesn't stay
in the source: the harvester sweeps every comment that isn't a dagger, a directive or a `// why:`
into the enclosing symbol's gloss section and plants the dagger, and nothing is
deleted to satisfy lint: the spillway fills by machine.

The calm default is harvest-at-commit (`gloss harvest --staged` in pre-commit). `gloss watch` is
opt-in per dev process and heavily debounced. It must never rewrite a file mid-edit, which is the
one real race here: an agent whose `Read` predates the harvest is holding drifted content.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#doctrine -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Doctrine (in "@inixiative/gloss")

#### Doctrine

**The gloss is advisory.** It is past-session commentary. It may be stale, it may have been wrong
when written. Trust the code over it. This is not a new cost: truth was never
enforceable for comments either, and comments carried no staleness signal at all. The gloss is held
to the standard comments always had, plus a derived freshness header they never had.

**Reading it is a second action**, like `git log` or `git blame`: prompted by a visible dagger and
felt confusion, not performed on every read. A gloss consulted 10% of the time still beats a comment
taxing 100% of reads.

**Never delete a gloss section or a dagger to green a failing check.** Run `gloss fix`. A check that
trains deletion gives the corpus a negative half-life: on every red rename, deleting the pair is the
cheapest green. Repair is built to be strictly cheaper than deletion, and the failure message says so.
